content: Malonic acid, also known by its IUPAC systematic name as propanedioic acid, is a dicarboxylic acid with the chemical structure CH₂(COOH)₂. The deprotonated form of malonic acid, along with its esters and salts, is referred to as malonates. For instance, diethyl malonate is the ethyl ester derivative of malonic acid. The name malonic is derived from the Latin word malum, meaning apple. Biochemistry The calcium salt of malonic acid is found in high concentrations in beetroot. Organic Synthesis A classical method for synthesizing malonic acid begins with acetic acid. Acetic acid is first chlorinated to produce chloroacetic acid. This compound is then treated with sodium carbonate to form its sodium salt, which subsequently undergoes a nucleophilic substitution reaction with sodium cyanide to yield the sodium salt of cyanoacetic acid. The nitrile group in this intermediate can be hydrolyzed using sodium hydroxide to produce sodium malonate. Acidification of sodium malonate then results in the formation of malonic acid. Organic Reactions In a well-known reaction, malonic acid condenses with urea to form barbituric acid. Additionally, malonic acid is frequently utilized as an enolate in Knoevenagel condensation reactions. It can also react with acetone to produce Meldrum's acid.
